## Summary
Document the ownership model and the expected show/hide behavior for the Gym SLL demo.

## User impact
Contributors can follow the documented pattern instead of adding more ad hoc chrome visibility logic.

## Minimal End-to-End Slice
- **Code**: No runtime code beyond doc-snippet consistency checks.
- **Tests**: Ensure any referenced commands or snippets match the real test targets.
- **Docs**: Update `example-games/gym/README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` with ownership/visibility guidance.
- **Infra**: Reuse the existing docs structure.
- **Observability**: Document how to confirm visibility behavior in the browser demo.

## Existing implementation to reuse
- Gym SLL sections in `example-games/gym/README.md`
- SLL guidance in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- browser tests for the Gym demo

## Acceptance Criteria
- Docs explain which mode shows which chrome.
- Docs explain how to register objects as shell-owned or scene-owned.
- Docs mention that Scene-only suppresses shared shell chrome.
- Documentation changes match the implemented behavior.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: Gym scene wiring (CG-0MPFM2MM4003OPP8).
- Parent: Suppress shared Gym help chrome in pure scene-only SLL views (CG-0MPFLM5EB009N5X8).

## Goal

Freeze the interfaces and pure logic for achievement-triggered game give-aways so the rest of the feature can be built and tested with no Steam, Electron, or real launcher.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GiveawayRule` (target game id + required achievement ids) and `GiveawayRuleSet` are typed and documented in `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts`; no game title is hard-coded in logic.
- Pure `evaluateGiveaways(unlockedAchievementIds, rules, alreadyUnlockedGameIds)` returns `{ gameId, unlocked, reason, missingAchievementIds }[]` with a discriminated `reason`.
- A unified multi-game `ContentUnlockStore` (memory + file implementation, corrupt-file-safe) generalises the existing single-game `UnlockStore`; the file store never throws.
- Unit tests cover: all required achievements met unlocks once; a subset blocks with `missingAchievementIds`; idempotent repeat; unknown/empty config is a no-op; a corrupt file degrades to empty state.
- Tests pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts` (new) — types + pure evaluation.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` — share the persistence store as a multi-game store.
- `tests/steam-giveaways/giveaway-contract.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Contract module, unified multi-game unlock store, unit tests.
data.title: Give-away unlock contract and deterministic fakes (test-first)

data.description:
## Goal

Make "won a game" a first-class, engine-generic achievement event so the give-away triggers have a real, Steam-free source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AchievementSystem` (or a documented thin extension) gains an idempotent game-outcome surface (e.g. `onGameOutcome({ gameId, outcome })`) that unlocks mapped achievements via the existing `AchievementSink`; zero Steam/Electron imports.
- The launcher manifest defines `first-win` and `second-distinct-game-win` meta-achievements (titles, descriptions, hidden flags) and the outcome-to-achievement mapping is engine-generic.
- "Second distinct game" logic only unlocks after wins in two different game ids; re-wins of the same game do not.
- `SteamAchievementService` idempotence and offline paths are reused unchanged for the meta-achievements.
- Unit tests cover outcome-to-unlock, distinct-game counting, idempotence, and no-op for unknown outcomes; pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`
- `src/core-engine/index.ts`
- `electron/achievement-manifest.json`
- `tests/steam-achievements/achievement-outcome.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Engine outcome surface, manifest meta-achievements, unit tests.
data.title: Engine game-outcome surface and cross-game meta-achievements

# Cross-repo icon wiring verification

**Parent:** CG-0MUUFZSE90061KKL.

## Goal

Independently verify, across all eight sibling game repos, that the icon wiring
landed correctly and record the evidence on the core work item.

## Scope

- For each affected repo: check `index.html` declares the three base-relative
  icon links; check every referenced `public/` icon file exists and resolves;
  check `./core` is at or after the icon commit.
- Run `npm run build` and the repo's test suite in each repo at the recorded
  commit.
- Record a coverage table (repo, `./core` pin, icon links present, public files
  present, test/build result, pushed commit hash) as a comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Cross-repo verification: every affected game repo's `index.html` declares the three base-relative icon links and each referenced `public/` icon file exists/resolves; every repo's `./core` pin is at or after the icon commit (CG-0MUTTXRWZ009NUB9); and each touched repo's full test suite passes.
- Each of the eight repos passes `npm run build` and its test suite at the recorded commit.
- A coverage table (repo, `./core` pin, icon links present, public files present, test/build result, pushed commit hash) is recorded as a comment on this work item.
- Any repo that fails is linked to a follow-up work item; no repo is left silently unverified.

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria above are met and verified on the recorded commits.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — the linkage mechanism under verification.
- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` — expected `sharedPublicRoot` list.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — the documented base-relative convention.
- `public/favicon.svg` — authoritative icon artefact.
data.title: Cross-repo icon wiring verification
